questions.text: Where did Apai Raushan grow up?
questions.hint: The reading says she lived in "a small village near Oral" as a child.

questions.text: Apai Raushan's family always had a television when she was young.
questions.hint: The text says "There was no television, no internet, and no mobile phones."

questions.text: How long did Apai Raushan work as a teacher?
questions.hint: "I taught primary school children for forty years."

questions.text: During the 1969 flood, Apai Raushan helped neighbours carry ___ to higher ground.
questions.hint: She "helped her neighbours carry their furniture to higher ground."

questions.text: What did Apai Raushan give Kamila at the end of the visit?
questions.hint: "Apai Raushan gave her an old black-and-white photograph."

questions.text: Apai Raushan is in the photograph — third from the right.
questions.hint: "That is me — third from the left," said Apai Raushan.

questions.text: The phrase "from scratch" means:
questions.hint: "From scratch" = starting with nothing prepared, using basic ingredients.

questions.text: Why did Pushkin visit Uralsk in 1833?
opts: To give lectures at the university
questions.hint: Dr. Akhmetov explained that Pushkin came to research a historical uprising.

questions.text: Zhibek had studied the Pugachev Rebellion at school before the museum visit.
questions.hint: Zhibek said: "I didn't study that in school yet."

questions.text: What happened to the Pugachev Rebellion leader in 1774?
questions.hint: "The government captured him in 1774. He was executed in Moscow."

questions.text: What was carved onto the sword handle?
questions.hint: "His name was carved onto the handle — can you see it?"

questions.text: The inscription on the sword was written in an old form of ___.
questions.hint: Dr. Akhmetov said it was "an old form of Cyrillic."

questions.text: Amir planned to tell his parents about the museum.
questions.hint: "I'm going to tell my parents about this place tonight."

questions.text: She ___ in a village when she was a child.
questions.hint: Past Simple positive: live + d = lived (ends in -e, add -d only).

questions.text: Kamila ___ (not study) on Saturday — she visited her grandmother.
questions.hint: Past Simple negative: didn't + BASE form (study).

questions.text: Which Past Simple spelling is correct?
questions.hint: study: consonant + y → change y to -ied.

questions.text: ___ Apai Raushan enjoy teaching? — Yes, she ___.
questions.hint: Question: Did + subject + base form. Short answer: Yes, she did.

questions.text: He ___ (stop) the car and looked at the old building.
questions.hint: stop: short CVC verb → double the final consonant → stopped.

questions.text: Amir ___ to the museum with Zhibek.
questions.hint: go → went (completely irregular).

questions.text: Dr. Akhmetov ___ them the history of the sword.
questions.hint: tell → told (irregular).

questions.text: Zhibek ___ (not know) about the rebellion before the visit.
questions.hint: Negative: didn't + BASE form. Base of 'knew' is 'know'.

questions.text: Kamila ___ (feel) proud when she saw the old photograph.
questions.hint: feel → felt (irregular).

questions.text: Pushkin ___ (write) a famous book about the Pugachev Rebellion.
questions.hint: write → wrote (irregular).

questions.text: A person who buys and sells goods for profit is called a:
questions.hint: A merchant = a person who trades goods commercially.

questions.text: "Courage" means the ability to face difficult situations without fear.
questions.hint: Courage = the ability to do something difficult despite fear.

questions.text: What does "cook from scratch" mean?
questions.hint: "From scratch" = starting from nothing prepared.

questions.text: An "artefact" is:
opts: A historical object made by humans
questions.correct: A historical object made by humans
questions.hint: Artefact = an object made by a person, especially an ancient one.

questions.text: A "rebellion" is a peaceful celebration.
questions.hint: A rebellion = an attempt to overthrow or resist authority (by force).

questions.text: The word "strict" describes a teacher who:
questions.hint: Strict = demanding obedience and discipline; not lenient.

questions.text: The commander's name was ___ onto the handle of the sword.
questions.hint: Carved = cut into a surface. "His name was carved onto the handle."
